idiom_name: sealed interface Node + records + record patterns; path as a List<Frame>
implementation_notes: A sealed interface plus records gives the algebraic tree, record patterns and an exhaustive switch make navigation and rebuild total, and List.copyOf/List.of supply the unmodifiable child list - so records replace the clone-and-copy-constructor boilerplate of a classic immutable class and switch over a sealed type replaces dynamic dispatch. The context stays hand-written: a List<Frame> where each frame holds the parent record and the child index. Prefer this form over the classic mutable Node hierarchy whenever the tree is a value shared between threads or versions; keep the mutable form when a UI model is updated in place under a single thread.
pitfalls: Record equals/hashCode are deep and recursive: putting locations or nodes in a HashSet or HashMap walks the entire subtree and can StackOverflowError on deep trees.
Records are only reference-immutable - a List field can still be mutated by whoever owns the list, so children must be defensively copied (List.copyOf) or held as immutable collections.
subList returns a view, not a copy: keeping the derived path alive keeps the parent list reachable, and the returned Loc should copy it (List.copyOf) before publishing.
Pattern matching over the sealed hierarchy is exhaustive, but a cast or a leaked mutable ArrayList defeats the guarantee at runtime.

variants.name: functionaljava TreeZipper over fj.data.Tree
variants.idiom_name: fj.data.TreeZipper (lefts, rights and a stream of parent contexts)
variants.implementation_notes: The pattern is shipped by a library: fj.data.Tree is the immutable tree and fj.data.TreeZipper is the location, holding the focused tree, the left and right sibling forests and a stream of parent contexts; parent(), left(), right() and firstChild() return Option<TreeZipper>, root() walks back to the top and treeZipper() constructs an edited location. Choose it when the project already uses functionaljava (its P4/Stream/Option types then appear in the API anyway); otherwise the sealed-records form keeps the model in plain JDK types.
pitfalls: The library builds on its own vocabulary (P4, Stream, Option) and pulls functionaljava into the module graph, which leaks into public signatures.
Every move returns Option: unwrapping with get() at the first convenient place is how the partiality discipline is lost.
Tree and zipper equality is structural, so comparing zippers is O(size) and unsuitable for hot paths or hashed collections.
